subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Should enabled Admin HTTP RPC routes reject untrusted browser-origin requests even when gateway.auth.mode="none" is explicitly configured for trusted private ingress?
rationale: The documented no-auth mode deliberately delegates trust to ingress topology, while existing gateway security work favors rejecting browser-origin requests without breaking origin-less host clients; choosing whether that rule applies universally is a security and compatibility policy decision.

options.title: Reject browser origins
options.body: Reject untrusted Origin headers and browser-simple mutation requests while preserving origin-less host automation in every auth mode.

options.title: Remove no-auth access
options.body: Require bearer or identity-bearing authentication for Admin HTTP RPC, accepting a compatibility break for existing private-ingress automation.

options.title: Preserve ingress trust
options.body: Keep no-auth behavior unchanged and document that operators must prevent browsers and untrusted origins from reaching the route.

recommendation.title: Reject browser origins
recommendation.body: Reject untrusted Origin headers and browser-simple mutation requests while preserving origin-less host automation in every auth mode.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work established browser-origin policy for authenticated Gateway HTTP operator routes while explicitly preserving headless clients.
